title: Behold, Crawzilla, the Not-Quite-Biggest Crayfish Ever Caught - Nautilus
gist: A teaser about a study in Ecology that began after a University of Illinois scientist caught an unusually large crayfish and a colleague claimed he had caught bigger. The study uses the debate to look at crayfish body size. The excerpt contains no findings.

insights.claim: A study published in Ecology on crayfish body size began as a bragging contest between colleagues, not as planned research.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Some research questions start from serendipity, a weak reminder that unplanned inquiry can still produce publishable work.
insights.quote: some comes from goofing off with your coworkers. A new study published in the journal Ecology is the latter

insights.claim: Caitlin Bloomer of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign caught a very large crayfish she thought might set a record, but a colleague said he had caught bigger ones.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Anecdotal claims about size are unreliable without systematic measurement, a general point about the quality of evidence.
insights.quote: he took one look and said, ‘No way, I’ve caught bigger.’
